 © 2026 Yahoo. All rights reserved. Leylah Fernandez's boyfriend, Vincent Boily, showed his support for the Canadian after she reached the semifinals of the Ningbo Open.
 Fernandez secured her place in the last four on Friday after defeating Ekaterina Alexandrova in the quarterfinals. Although she lost the opening set 4-6, the Canadian bounced back strongly, winning the next two sets by earning four service breaks without allowing Alexandrova a break point during that stretch.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement The 4-6, 6-2, 6-1 victory also brought Fernandez's career head-to-head record against Alexandrova to 3-3. It was her second win over the Russian in two weeks, following another three-set victory at the Wuhan Open. After the match, Fernandez shared several pictures from the tournament on Instagram and celebrated her quarterfinal victory, writing:
 "Onto the semis. Let's go Ningbo!!!"
 Boily, who is a Canadian ice sled hockey player, responded to the post with a brief message of encouragement, commenting:
 "Yesss🙌"
 Boily's comment on Fernandez's post (Image via Instagram/ @leylahfernandez)
 Fernandez and Boily reportedly began dating after the Canadian playfully invited fans to contact her for a one-hour coffee date in July 2025. They made their relationship public in May 2026, when Fernandez shared romantic pictures from their vacation in Rome.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Leylah Fernandez reflects on her quarterfinal victory over Ekaterina Alexandrova at the Ningbo Open
 After winning her Ningbo Open quarterfinal against Ekaterina Alexandrova on Friday, Leylah Fernandez spoke to reporters during the post-match press conference about the showdown. She discussed the challenge of facing Alexandrova and explained how she adjusted her game after a difficult opening set.
 "I knew Ekaterina, she was going to come in strong. I don't think it's necessarily because of the roof. I think it's just the, you know, she's also a competitor. Last time we played each other, it may not have been her best of match. So I'm sure she came in with a lot of motivation, and I knew that from the get-go. So, you know, seeing feeling how she was attacking, and I was a little bit too passive, too kind of gave her the upper hand," said Fernandez.
 She added:
 "But I was actually pretty proud with myself on how I didn't let that kind of deter me and just keep fighting, keep finding solutions."
 Leylah Fernandez entered the Ningbo Open after competing at the Wuhan Open, where she lost to Jelena Ostapenko in the round of 16 on October 15.
